problem: Realistic PointGoal navigation (noisy depth and actuation, no GPS+Compass) breaks end-to-end RL agents. They make progress toward the goal but cannot self-localize, so they fail to stop precisely at it.
motivation: Ground-truth localization is unrealistic in unseen real environments, yet DD-PPO only 'solves' PointNav with it. Learning navigation and tracking jointly is circular: better tracking enables a better policy, which shifts the input distribution and degrades tracking.
key_idea: Serialize learning of navigation and localization by giving the agent GPS+Compass as privileged training-time information through a KL-penalized information bottleneck, and add ego-motion and self-tracking auxiliary losses so it learns to localize itself.
insight: The auxiliary losses account for nearly all of the gain: without them SPL stays at 10.95, while adding them gives 58.29 (semi-idealized, 120M steps). Soft-SPL stays high without them, so the agents navigate fine but cannot stop precisely, meaning localization is the bottleneck. The information bottleneck adds modest gains (SPL 58.29 to 59.68) and better sample efficiency and lower tracking error. It needs a large fixed beta: beta=1 or annealing makes the agent rely on privileged information and fail at test time.
method: Visual/state encoder: a frozen ResNet-18 pretrained on PointNav with GPS+Compass encodes two consecutive depth frames into a visual embedding E_v (384-d) and a flow embedding E_f (128-d) from the embedding difference; a 2-layer LSTM outputs the belief state b_t.

Information bottleneck: an MLP maps [b_t, embedding of the GT-updated goal] to N(mu, sigma) for a latent Z, with a beta*KL(p(Z|G,S)||N(0,I)) penalty (beta=10, KL subsampled to 20%); at test time Z is sampled from the prior N(0,I).

Self-tracking auxiliary losses: MLP heads on b_t predict position and heading (MSE and angular distance); the predicted pose updates the PointGoal fed to the policy head, which is needed for a reliable STOP.
Ego-motion auxiliary loss: an MLP on E_f predicts the change in position and heading between consecutive frames.
Dynamic success reward (DSR): stop reward multiplied by 2.5*exp((R_PG - dist)/R_PG), which pushes the agent to stop near the center of the success zone.
Training: DD-PPO on 8 GPUs, 300M steps (semi-idealized) or 350M steps (realistic), Gibson scenes.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 depth encoder (frozen, pretrained with GPS+Compass) + 2-layer LSTM policy, trained with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: Gibson scenes in Habitat, RL only, 300M-350M steps of experience; visual encoder pretrained on PointNav with GPS+Compass
setting.observation: egocentric depth only at test time (two consecutive 360x640 frames); GPS+Compass available only at training time via the bottleneck
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: stop, move_forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°
setting.privileged: GT GPS+Compass used only during training via the information bottleneck; none at test time

results: In the semi-idealized setting the method reaches 68.87 SPL / 75.05 SR, beating Datta et al. (50.80 / 53.50) by +18.07 SPL. In the realistic setting it reaches 19.86 SPL / 26.66 SR on val, +15.41 SPL over Datta et al., though Datta's numbers were obtained with perfect sensing. On the Habitat Challenge 2020 test set it gets 12.2 SPL, only slightly above Datta (11.9) and well below the later VO (52.5) and DAN (37.7) approaches, which are far slower at inference.
limitations: Absolute realistic-setting performance is low (12.2 SPL on the test set) and far below later map- or odometry-based methods on the leaderboard.
The bottleneck needs a large fixed beta; small beta or annealing fails to generalize, and the gain from the bottleneck is modest.
Some baseline comparisons are not like-for-like: Datta et al. numbers used perfect sensing and a large-scale 128-GPU setup.
